country.name: Namibia
country.tagline: A few desert-edge wineries in a country better known for its Orange River table grapes.

stats.note: A handful of small wineries; most Namibian grapes are table grapes for export.

country.overview: Namibia is one of the driest countries on earth and lies largely north of the traditional wine belt, but a few people have made wine there for over a century. German Catholic priests planted vines in Klein Windhoek in the 1890s, making white wine and a schnapps called 'Katholischer' until the 1960s. After independence in 1990, Helmuth Kluge started Kristall Kellerei at Omaruru, growing Colombard and Ruby Cabernet (it now focuses on brandy and fruit wines). In the 1990s Allen Walkden-Davis planted Shiraz at Neuras, a spring-fed oasis near Maltahöhe at the edge of the Namib-Naukluft, which may be the driest vineyard in the world; Thonningii in the Otavi Mountains and Erongo Mountain Winery followed. Large irrigated table-grape farms along the Orange River at Aussenkehr export to Europe.

history.title: Klein Windhoek mission vines
history.text: German Catholic priests planted the first vineyards in Klein Windhoek; production stopped in the late 1960s.

history.title: Kristall Kellerei
history.text: Helmuth Kluge began making wine at Omaruru in the year of independence.

history.title: Neuras
history.text: Allen Walkden-Davis planted Shiraz at the Neuras oasis near Maltahöhe, on the edge of the Namib.

country.climate_soils: Arid, sunny and hot with cold nights; irrigation from springs and boreholes; vineyards between about 900 and 1,500 m.

grapes.name: Shiraz
grapes.note: The main red at Neuras and Thonningii.

sites.name: Kristall Kellerei
sites.text: A small winery and distillery at Omaruru, started by Helmuth Kluge in 1990 with Colombard and Ruby Cabernet. Now best known for brandy and fruit wines, it was a pioneer of post-independence Namibian wine.

sites.name: Neuras
sites.text: A spring-fed oasis farm near Maltahöhe at the edge of the Namib-Naukluft, where Allen Walkden-Davis planted Shiraz in the 1990s. With almost no rain, it is one of the driest vineyards in the world and now belongs to a wildlife conservation foundation.
